sentences.text: Rothia species are Gram-positive cocco-bacilli placed in the family Micrococcaceae.
They are regarded as part of the normal microflora of the human mouth and upper respiratory tract.
Oral isolates typed as Rothia mucilaginosa and Rothia aeria showed high gluten-degrading activity, identifying the genus as a natural coloniser of the upper gastro-intestinal tract.
Rothia mucilaginosa is also often detectable in the lower airways in chronic lung disease, where it inhibited pathogen- and lipopolysaccharide-induced pro-inflammatory responses in laboratory models.
Reviews describe the genus as an emerging opportunistic pathogen, and bacteraemia has been reported mainly in neutropenic patients with haematological malignancy.
